## Welcome & Agenda

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Knowledge Mobilization (KMb)

> Purposeful activities that facilitate the **creation, sharing, uptake,
> and use** of research knowledge to inform **practice, policy, systems,
> and the public good**.

Can be two-way (not just pushing information) and start at at the design
stage (not just at the end)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## KMb Fits in the Research Cycle

1.  **Co-define questions** with stakeholders
2.  **Co-design methods & materials** (surveys, protocols, instruments)
3.  **Sense-making** during analysis (member checks, workshops)
4.  **Share & adapt** products to audience context
5.  **Evaluate & iterate** (what changed? for whom?)

::: notes
Emphasize iteration and relational work; it’s not a single deliverable.
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Who are your audiences

-   Other researchers
-   Practitioners: librarians, archivists, records managers
-   Decision/policy makers: library boards, university admins, funders,
    government
-   Organizations: professional associations, media, NGOs
-   Communities: patrons, underrepresented groups, Indigenous
    communities

Think of a few stakeholders for your project and why your project might
matter to them.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Knowledge mobilization plan

-   Objectives
-   Audiences & needs
-   Channels/products
-   Timeline & responsibilities
-   Resources & budget
-   Evaluation

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Matching Audiences to Channels

| Audience | Need/Interest | Formats | Channels |
|------------------|------------------|------------------|------------------|
| Public library directors | Program or budget choices | 1–2 page brief, dashboard snapshot | Email via association list, webinar |
| Frontline librarians | Implementation guidance | Checklist, how-to, workshop | In-service training, conference session |
| Policy makers | High-level options | Policy note with options/risks | Meetings, stakeholder roundtables |
| Researchers | Methods & evidence | Article, preprint, dataset/code | OA journal, repository (e.g., OSF, Dataverse) |
| Communities | Local relevance | Plain-language summary, zine, posters | Community events, social media |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Examples of formats

-   Plain-language summary
-   Policy brief
-   Slide deck
-   Podcast
-   Video
-   Infographic
-   Workshop
-   Dataset
-   Code
-   Preprint
-   Blogpost
-   Interactive dashboard

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Evaluation

-   **Reach**: views, downloads, attendees, media hits, social shares
-   **Usefulness**: stakeholder feedback, satisfaction, intention to use
-   **Uptake/influcence**: citations in policy docs, protocol changes,
    new pilots
-   **Outcomes**: measured changes, cost/time savings

**How to collect the data?** surveys, interviews, metrics, etc.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Example

**Study**: Impact of extended weekend hours on student success in an
academic library.

-   **Audiences**: Provost, library staff, student union
-   **Products**: 2-page decision brief (Provost); checklist & training
    session (staff); plain-language summary & infographic (students)
-   **Timeline**: Interim results mid-term; final at semester end;
    follow-up at 6 months
-   **Evaluation**: Brief downloads; policy memo citation; attendance at
    staff session; change in gate counts & student feedback

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Another example

**Study**: Digital literacy program effectiveness for older adults.

-   **Audiences**: City council, program coordinators, community centers
-   **Products**: Policy note with options; facilitator guide; community
    posters (large-font)
-   **Equity**: Transportation stipends, large-print materials,
    translation
-   **Evaluation**: Pre/post skill measures; adoption by 3 centers;
    testimonials
